extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys/agents, receiving/designated/elected national patent Offices, International Searching Authorities, and International Preliminary Examining Authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive/procedural criteria governing filing, processing, publication, confidentiality, amendment, international preliminary examination, and national/elected Office treatment of PCT international applications. Covers when effects are lost/maintained, what documentation/translations/fees are required, and the standard of the international preliminary examination (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible loss of effect in designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the international application provided for in Article 11(3) shall cease in any designated State with the same consequences as the withdrawal of any national application in that State if: (i) the applicant withdraws his international application or the designation of that State; (ii) the international application is considered withdrawn by virtue of Articles 12(3), 14(1)(b), 14(3)(a), or 14(4), or if the designation of that State is considered withdrawn by virtue of Article 14(3)(b); (iii) the applicant fails to perform the acts referred to in Article 22 within the applicable time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding these grounds for cessation, a designated Office may maintain the effect provided for in Article 11(3) even where not required by Article 25(2). See also editorial notes concerning varying national incompatibilities with Article 22 time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Office review and correction rights (Article 25/26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office has refused to accord an international filing date, declared the international application considered withdrawn, or the IB has made a finding under Article 12(3), the IB shall promptly send copies of any document in the file to any designated Office named by the applicant at the applicant's request. Designated Offices shall decide whether the refusal, declaration or finding was justified and, if due to error/omission by the receiving Office or IB, treat the international application as if such error/omission had not occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for copies must be presented within prescribed time limits; national fee and appropriate translation (if any) must be paid/furnished within prescribed limits. If record copy reached IB late because of applicant error, corrective treatment is limited per Article 48(2). Designated Offices must give applicants opportunity to correct applications under procedures comparable to national law before rejecting for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to correct before designated Offices / obligation to allow correction
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall reject an international application on the grounds of non-compliance with the requirements of this Treaty and the Regulations without first giving the applicant the opportunity to correct the said application to the extent and according to the procedure provided by the national law for the same or comparable situations in respect of national applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory procedural protection — designated Offices must follow national correction procedures (or comparable ones) prior to rejection for form/content non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: National law shall not add form/content requirements (Article 27(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: No national law shall require compliance with requirements relating to the form or contents of the international application different from or additional to those which are provided for in this Treaty and the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions and qualifications follow: see Article 27(2)-(8) for permitted documentary/formal requirements and for substantive patentability freedom (States remain free to apply substantive conditions of patentability). National Offices may, after processing starts, require names of officers (for legal entities), documentary proof of statements (e.g., confirmation/signature), representation/address requirements, or other national security/economic measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection where filer not qualified under national law (Article 27(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant, for the purposes of any designated State, is not qualified according to the national law of that State to file a national application because he is not the inventor, the international application may be rejected by the designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit ground for national rejection despite Treaty-form requirements; applicants should check national qualification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Contracting States to set substantive patentability conditions (Article 27(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Treaty and the Regulations is intended to be construed as prescribing anything that would limit the freedom of each Contracting State to prescribe such substantive conditions of patentability as it desires. Definitions of prior art in this Treaty are exclusively for international procedure purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting States may apply their own criteria for prior art and other substantive conditions when determining patentability nationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments before designated/elected Offices (Articles 28 & 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall be given the opportunity to amend the claims, the description, and the drawings, before each designated (Article 28) and each elected Office (Article 41) within the prescribed time limit. No designated/elected Office shall grant or refuse a patent before such time limit has expired except with the express consent of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed, unless the national law of the designated/elected State permits. Amendments must conform to national law for matters not covered by the Treaty/Regulations. Where a translation is required, amendments shall be in the language of the translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of the international publication (Article 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as protection of any rights of the applicant in a designated State is concerned, effects of international publication shall, subject to paragraphs (2)-(4), be the same as those which the national law of the designated State provides for compulsory national publication of unexamined national applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication language differs from national publication language, national law may make those effects applicable only from publication/translation availability/transmission to possible infringers or combinations thereof. National law may also defer effects to 18 months from priority date if requested by applicant, or to the date a copy is received in the national Office (which must be published in that Office's gazette).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential nature of the international application (Article 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau and the International Searching Authorities shall not allow access to the international application before international publication unless requested/authorized by the applicant. No national Office shall allow access to the international application by third parties, unless requested/authorized by the applicant, before the earliest of: (i) international publication; (ii) receipt of communication under Article 20; (iii) receipt of a copy under Article 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: transmittals to competent ISAs, Article 13 transmittals, communications under Article 20, judicial access, and limited public notice that an Office was designated (restricted data: receiving Office ID, applicant name, intl filing date/number, title). 'Access' covers any means (individual communication or general publication). National Offices should not publish an international application or translation generally before international publication or, if publication has not occurred by 20 months from priority, before 20 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for International Preliminary Examination — formal requirements (Article 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand for international preliminary examination must be made separately from the international application, contain the prescribed particulars, and be in the prescribed language and form. It shall indicate elected States (those in which applicant intends to use results). The demand is subject to payment of prescribed fees within prescribed time limits and must be submitted to the competent International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants resident or national of States bound by Chapter II (or persons allowed by Assembly decision) may make a demand; additional elections may be made later but only for States already designated under Article 4. Each elected Office shall be notified of its election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective and criteria of the International Preliminary Examination (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective is to formulate a preliminary and non‑binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step (to be non‑obvious), and to be industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international preliminary examination purposes: novelty = not anticipated by prior art as defined in the Regulations; inventive step = not obvious to a person skilled in the art at the prescribed relevant date; industrial applicability = can be made or used in any kind of industry (industry in broad sense). These criteria serve only for international preliminary examination; Contracting States may apply additional or different criteria nationally. Examination shall consider all documents cited in the international search report and may consider additional relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitations for IPEA (Article 34(4) & 35(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA considers the application relates to subject matter on which it is not required to carry out an international preliminary examination, or that description/claims/drawings are so unclear or inadequately supported that no meaningful opinion can be formed on novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability, the Authority shall not go into those questions and shall inform the applicant with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these situations exist only for certain claims, the Authority's limitation applies to those claims only. The IPEA's report in such cases shall state this opinion and reasons, and shall not contain the usual claim-by-claim statements under Article 35(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant rights in the international preliminary examination procedure (Article 34(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall have the right to communicate orally and in writing with the IPEA; the right to amend claims, description and drawings in prescribed manner and time before the report is established (amendments not beyond disclosure); receive at least one written opinion unless conditions in Article 34(2)(c) are met; and the right to respond to the written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 34(2)(c) lists conditions under which no written opinion is necessary (invention satisfies Article 33(1) criteria, application complies with Treaty/Regulations as checked, and no observations intended under Article 35(2) last sentence). For lack of unity, IPEA may invite restriction of claims or payment of additional fees; national law may treat unselected parts as withdrawn unless special national fees are paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and limits of the International Preliminary Examination Report (Article 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report shall be established within prescribed time and form and shall not state whether the invention is or seems patentable under any national law. It shall state, for each claim, whether the claim appears to satisfy the criteria of novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability as defined for international preliminary examination, accompanied by citation of supporting documents and explanations and other observations as provided in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Article 34(4)(a) situation exists, the report shall state that opinion and reasons and shall not contain the Article 35(2) statements. If only some claims are affected, the report should mix the appropriate statements for affected and unaffected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal, translation, and communication of the IPR (Article 36)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international preliminary examination report and annexes shall be transmitted to the applicant and the International Bureau. The report and annexes shall be translated into prescribed languages: translations of the report are prepared by or under the responsibility of the International Bureau; translations of annexes by the applicant. The report with its translation and annexes in original language shall be communicated by the IB to each elected Office; prescribed translation of annexes must be transmitted by the applicant to elected Offices within prescribed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 20(3) applies mutatis mutandis to copies of any document cited in the IPR that was not cited in the international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of demand or election (Article 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw any or all elections; if election of all elected States is withdrawn, the demand is considered withdrawn. Withdrawals must be notified to the International Bureau; elected Offices and the IPEA will be notified accordingly. Withdrawal of the demand or election shall, unless national law provides otherwise, be considered withdrawal of the international application as far as that State is concerned (with specified exceptions relating to time limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing matters: withdrawal prior to expiration of applicable Article 22 time limit may not be considered withdrawal of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the international preliminary examination (Article 38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the International Bureau nor the IPEA shall, unless requested/authorized by the applicant, allow access to the file of the international preliminary examination by any person or authority at any time, except by elected Offices once the IPR has been established. Nor shall they give information on issuance/nonissuance of an IPR and on withdrawal/non-withdrawal of demand/election, except as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the confidentiality of the IPEA proceedings until the report is established and disseminated to elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy, translation and national fee requirements to elected Offices (Article 39)
rubrics_metrics.description: If election of any Contracting State is effected prior to expiration of the 19th month from the priority date, Article 22 does not apply to such State and the applicant shall furnish a copy of the international application (unless Article 20 communication already took place), a translation thereof (as prescribed), and pay the national fee (if any) to each elected Office not later than expiration of 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National law may set later time limits for performing these acts. Failure to perform the acts within the applicable time limit causes the effect in the elected State to cease with same consequences as withdrawal of a national application, unless the elected Office chooses to maintain the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delaying of national examination and other processing (Article 40)
rubrics_metrics.description: If election is effected prior to the 19th month, the national Office shall not proceed to examination and other processing prior to expiration of the applicable time limit under Article 39, subject to paragraph (2). However, any elected Office may, on the express request of the applicant, proceed to examination and other processing at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives applicants control to defer or accelerate national prosecution in elected Offices by their election timing and express requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of national examination in elected Offices — confidentiality between Offices (Article 42)
rubrics_metrics.description: No elected Office receiving the international preliminary examination report may require the applicant to furnish copies, or information on the contents, of any papers connected with the examination relating to the same international application in any other elected Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents cross‑office disclosure demands and protects applicant's papers from duplicated disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect translation remedy (Article 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, because of an incorrect translation of the international application, the scope of any patent granted on that application exceeds the scope of the international application in its original language, the competent authorities of the Contracting State concerned may retroactively limit the scope of the patent, and declare it null and void to the extent that its scope has exceeded the original-language scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National authorities have power to correct/limit/void patents where translation errors caused scope expansion beyond original language application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-limits governed by Regulations and modification procedure (Article 47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details for computing time limits referred to in this Treaty are governed by the Regulations. All time limits fixed in Chapters I and II may, outside revisions under Article 60, be modified by decision of the Contracting States; such decisions must be unanimous and made in the Assembly or through correspondence, with procedure details governed by the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and Offices must follow the Regulations for computing and applying time limits; changes require unanimous Contracting State decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in meeting time limits — excusable delays (Article 48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any time limit is not met because of interruption in the mail service or unavoidable loss/delay in the mail, the time limit shall be deemed met in the cases and subject to the proof and other conditions prescribed in the Regulations. Any Contracting State shall excuse delays for reasons admitted under its national law and may excuse delays for other reasons as far as that State is concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural relief for missed time limits depends on national law and Regulations; applicants should preserve proof and follow Regulations for relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to practice before International Authorities (Article 49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attorney, patent agent, or other person having the right to practice before the national Office with which the international application was filed shall be entitled to practice before the International Bureau and the competent ISAs and IPEAs in respect of that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves representation rights before international authorities for those authorized before the receiving national Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information services and technical assistance (Articles 50–51)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau may provide patent information services (directly or through ISAs or specialized institutions) to facilitate acquisition of technical knowledge, particularly for developing countries. The Assembly shall establish a Committee for Technical Assistance to organize and supervise technical assistance of training, experts, and equipment supply to developing Contracting States; financing and implementation details governed by Assembly decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services to governments furnished at cost, and to developing country governments below cost where subsidized; Assembly may make services available to others and recommend financing methods.
